1	<purpose>
2	Cross-AI peer review — invoke external AI CLIs to independently review phase plans.
3	Each CLI gets the same prompt (PROJECT.md context, phase plans, requirements) and
4	produces structured feedback. Results are combined into REVIEWS.md for the planner
5	to incorporate via --reviews flag. The synthesis is a consumer contract, not a soft
6	consensus summary: lone high-signal criticism, merely-adequate areas, and later-audit
7	risks stay visible even when they are not majority views.
8	
9	This implements adversarial review: different AI models catch different blind spots.
10	A plan that survives review from 2-3 independent AI systems is more robust.
11	</purpose>
12	
13	<process>
14	
15	<step name="detect_clis">
16	Check which AI CLIs are available on the system:
17	
18	```bash
19	# Check each CLI
20	command -v gemini >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "gemini:available" || echo "gemini:missing"
21	command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "claude:available" || echo "claude:missing"
22	command -v codex >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "codex:available" || echo "codex:missing"
23	command -v coderabbit >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "coderabbit:available" || echo "coderabbit:missing"
24	command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "opencode:available" || echo "opencode:missing"
25	```
26	
27	Parse flags from `{{GSD_ARGS}}`:
28	- `--gemini` → include Gemini
29	- `--claude` → include the agent
30	- `--codex` → include Codex
31	- `--coderabbit` → include CodeRabbit
32	- `--opencode` → include OpenCode
33	- `--all` → include all available
34	- No flags → include all available
35	
36	If no CLIs are available:
37	```
38	No external AI CLIs found. Install at least one:
39	- gemini: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli
40	- codex: https://github.com/openai/codex
41	- claude: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code
42	- opencode: https://opencode.ai (leverages GitHub Copilot subscription models)
43	
44	Then run /gsd-review again.
45	```
46	Exit.
47	
48	Determine which CLI to skip based on the current runtime environment:
49	
50	```bash
51	# Environment-based runtime detection (priority order)
52	if [ "$ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT" = "1" ]; then
53	  # Antigravity is a separate client — all CLIs are external, skip none
54	  SELF_CLI="none"
55	elif [ -n "$CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT" ]; then
56	  # Running inside Claude Code CLI — skip claude for independence
57	  SELF_CLI="claude"
58	else
59	  # Other environments (Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, etc.)
60	  # Fall back to AI self-identification to decide which CLI to skip
61	  SELF_CLI="auto"
62	fi
63	```
64	
65	Rules:
66	- If `SELF_CLI="none"` → invoke ALL available CLIs (no skip)

<purpose>
Cross-AI peer review — invoke external AI CLIs to independently review phase plans.
Each CLI gets the same prompt (PROJECT.md context, phase plans, requirements) and
produces structured feedback. Results are combined into REVIEWS.md for the planner
to incorporate via --reviews flag. The synthesis is a consumer contract, not a soft
consensus summary: lone high-signal criticism, merely-adequate areas, and later-audit
risks stay visible even when they are not majority views.

This implements adversarial review: different AI models catch different blind spots.
A plan that survives review from 2-3 independent AI systems is more robust.
</purpose>

<process>

<step name="detect_clis">
Check which AI CLIs are available on the system:

```bash
# Check each CLI
command -v gemini >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "gemini:available" || echo "gemini:missing"
command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "claude:available" || echo "claude:missing"
command -v codex >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "codex:available" || echo "codex:missing"
command -v coderabbit >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "coderabbit:available" || echo "coderabbit:missing"
command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "opencode:available" || echo "opencode:missing"
```

Parse flags from `{{GSD_ARGS}}`:
- `--gemini` → include Gemini
- `--claude` → include the agent
- `--codex` → include Codex
- `--coderabbit` → include CodeRabbit
- `--opencode` → include OpenCode
- `--all` → include all available
- No flags → include all available

If no CLIs are available:
```
No external AI CLIs found. Install at least one:
- gemini: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli
- codex: https://github.com/openai/codex
- claude: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code
- opencode: https://opencode.ai (leverages GitHub Copilot subscription models)

Then run /gsd-review again.
```
Exit.

Determine which CLI to skip based on the current runtime environment:

```bash
# Environment-based runtime detection (priority order)
if [ "$ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT" = "1" ]; then
  # Antigravity is a separate client — all CLIs are external, skip none
  SELF_CLI="none"
elif [ -n "$CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT" ]; then
  # Running inside Claude Code CLI — skip claude for independence
  SELF_CLI="claude"
else
  # Other environments (Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, etc.)
  # Fall back to AI self-identification to decide which CLI to skip
  SELF_CLI="auto"
fi
```

Rules:
- If `SELF_CLI="none"` → invoke ALL available CLIs (no skip)
- If `SELF_CLI="claude"` → skip claude, use gemini/codex
- If `SELF_CLI="auto"` → the executing AI identifies itself and skips its own CLI
- At least one DIFFERENT CLI must be available for the review to proceed.
</step>

<step name="gather_context">
Collect phase artifacts for the review prompt:

```bash
INIT=$(node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" init phase-op "${PHASE_ARG}")
if [[ "$INIT" == @file:* ]]; then INIT=$(cat "${INIT#@file:}"); fi
```

Read from init: `phase_dir`, `phase_number`, `padded_phase`.

1. `.planning/PROJECT.md` (first 80 lines — project context)

</step>

<step name="build_prompt">
Build a structured review prompt:

```markdown
# Cross-AI Plan Review Request

You are reviewing implementation plans for a software project phase.
Provide structured feedback on plan quality, completeness, and risks.

## Project Context
{first 80 lines of PROJECT.md}

## Phase {N}: {phase name}
### Roadmap Section
{roadmap phase section}

### Requirements Addressed
{requirements for this phase}

### User Decisions (CONTEXT.md)
{context if present}

### Research Findings
{research if present}

### Plans to Review
{all PLAN.md contents}

## Review Instructions

Analyze each plan and provide:

1. **Summary** — One-paragraph assessment
2. **Strongest Justified Criticism** — The single most important criticism you can defend, with severity and reasoning
3. **What Is Already Strong** — What's well-designed and should be preserved (bullet points)

5. **Concerns** — Potential issues, gaps, risks (bullet points with severity: HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
6. **Later Audit Failures** — What would likely fail a later stringent audit by strong engineers, designers, or researchers
7. **Suggestions** — Specific improvements (bullet points)
8. **Risk Assessment** — Overall risk level (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) with justification

Focus on:
- Missing edge cases or error handling
- Dependency ordering issues
- Scope creep or over-engineering
- Security considerations
- Performance implications
- Whether the plans actually achieve the phase goals
- What must change before a later strong-engineer audit could honestly pass

Output your review in markdown format.
```


**OpenCode (via GitHub Copilot):**

Display progress:

# Reviews Mode — Planner Reference

Triggered when orchestrator sets Mode to `reviews`. Replanning from scratch with REVIEWS.md feedback as additional context.

**Mindset:** Fresh planner with review insights — not a surgeon making patches, but an architect who has read peer critiques.

### Step 1: Load REVIEWS.md
Read the reviews file from `<files_to_read>`. Parse:
- Per-reviewer feedback (strengths, concerns, suggestions)
- Review Consumer Contract:
  - Must Address In Replan
  - Explicit Rebuttal Required If Not Accepted
  - Safe To Defer
- Review Synthesis:
  - Agreed Concerns
  - Lone High-Signal Concerns
  - Merely Adequate Areas
  - Later Audit Risks
  - Divergent Views
- Treat synthesis as guidance, not as permission to ignore a strong individual criticism.
- If the consumer-contract section is missing or incomplete, derive the same buckets from the individual reviews and synthesis instead of downgrading the review pass.

### Step 2: Categorize Feedback
Group review feedback into:
- **Must address**:
  - Every item in `Must Address In Replan`
  - HIGH severity agreed concerns
  - Any lone high-signal criticism that is well-justified and would create likely later-audit failure if ignored
  - Later audit risks or merely-adequate areas that would leave the plan weak, misleadingly closure-ready, or brittle against the repo quality bar if left untouched
- **Should address**:
  - MEDIUM severity agreed concerns
  - Merely adequate areas that leave the plan technically passable but weak for the repo's quality bar, when they are not already in Must address
- **Consider**:
  - Items listed in `Safe To Defer`
  - Individual reviewer suggestions that are useful but not load-bearing
  - LOW severity items
- **Explicit rebuttal required**:
  - Every item in `Explicit Rebuttal Required If Not Accepted`
- Consensus raises confidence, but lack of consensus does not automatically downgrade a criticism.

### Step 3: Plan Fresh with Review Context
Create new plans following the standard planning process, but with review feedback as additional constraints:
- Each must-address concern MUST have a task that addresses it or an explicit written rebuttal for why the criticism is not accepted
- MEDIUM concerns and merely-adequate areas should be addressed where feasible without over-engineering
- Note in task actions: "Addresses review concern: {concern}" for traceability
- If you reject a lone high-signal criticism, explain why the criticism is not persuasive; do not dismiss it solely because only one reviewer raised it
- Do not leave the existing plans materially unchanged unless you can point to the exact existing plan/task that already satisfies each must-address concern
- If a concern is already covered, say exactly which plan/task covers it instead of silently assuming coverage

### Step 4: Return
Use standard PLANNING COMPLETE return format, adding a reviews section:

```markdown
### Review Feedback Addressed

| Concern | Source | Severity | How Addressed |
|---------|--------|----------|---------------|
| {concern} | {reviewer or synthesis section} | HIGH | Plan {N}, Task {M}: {how} |

### Review Feedback Deferred
| Concern | Source | Reason |
|---------|--------|--------|
| {concern} | {reviewer or synthesis section} | {why — safe to defer or intentionally sequenced out} |

### Review Feedback Rejected
| Concern | Source | Reason |
|---------|--------|--------|
| {concern} | {reviewer or synthesis section} | {why the criticism was not accepted on the merits} |
```

792	## 9b. Handle Phase Split Recommendation
793	
794	When the planner returns `## PHASE SPLIT RECOMMENDED`, it means the phase has too many decisions to implement at full fidelity within the plan budget. The planner proposes groupings.
795	
796	**Extract from planner return:**
797	- Proposed sub-phases (e.g., "17a: processing core (D-01 to D-19)", "17b: billing + config UX (D-20 to D-27)")
798	- Which D-XX decisions go in each sub-phase
799	- Why the split is necessary (decision count, complexity estimate)
800	
801	**Present to user:**
802	```
803	## Phase {X} is too complex for full-fidelity implementation
804	
805	The planner found {N} decisions that cannot all be implemented without
806	simplifying some. Instead of reducing your decisions, we recommend splitting:
807	
808	**Option 1: Split into sub-phases**
809	- Phase {X}a: {name} — {D-XX to D-YY} ({N} decisions)
810	- Phase {X}b: {name} — {D-XX to D-YY} ({M} decisions)
811	
812	**Option 2: Proceed anyway** (planner will attempt all, quality may degrade)
813	
814	**Option 3: Prioritize** — you choose which decisions to implement now,
815	rest become a follow-up phase
816	```
817	
818	Use AskUserQuestion with these 3 options.
819	
820	**If "Split":** Use `/gsd-insert-phase` to create the sub-phases, then replan each.
821	**If "Proceed":** Return to planner with instruction to attempt all decisions at full fidelity, accepting more plans/tasks.
822	**If "Prioritize":** Use AskUserQuestion (multiSelect) to let user pick which D-XX are "now" vs "later". Create CONTEXT.md for each sub-phase with the selected decisions.
823	
824	## 10. Spawn gsd-plan-checker Agent
825	
826	Display banner:
827	```
828	━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
829	 GSD ► VERIFYING PLANS
830	━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
831	
832	◆ Spawning plan checker...
833	```
834	
835	Checker prompt:
836	
837	```markdown
838	<verification_context>
839	**Phase:** {phase_number}
840	**Phase Goal:** {goal from ROADMAP}
841	
842	<files_to_read>
843	- {PHASE_DIR}/*-PLAN.md (Plans to verify)
844	- {roadmap_path} (Roadmap)
845	- {requirements_path} (Requirements)
846	- {context_path} (Phase steering brief from /gsd-discuss-phase)
847	- {context_canonical_refs} (Resolved files from CONTEXT.md `<canonical_refs>` — MUST be read when present)
848	- {research_path} (Technical Research — includes Validation Architecture)
849	- {reviews_path} (Cross-AI Review Feedback — if --reviews)
850	</files_to_read>
851	
852	${AGENT_SKILLS_CHECKER}
853	
854	**Phase requirement IDs (MUST ALL be covered):** {phase_req_ids}
855	
856	Verification guidance:
857	- Flag plans that ignore material `<open_questions>` without resolving or sequencing them
858	- Flag plans that violate `<future_awareness>` or `<derived_constraints>`
859	- Flag plans that silently drop a material future-awareness item instead of preserving it, sequencing it, validating it, or explicitly justifying non-action now
860	- If context future-awareness is non-empty, fail plans whose `future_preservation` frontmatter is missing, empty, or generic enough to be non-auditable
861	- If context future-awareness includes `Strengthening Opportunities`, fail plans whose `future_preservation.strengthening_routes` is missing, empty, generic, or lacks a concrete seed handoff when the route is `explicit hold-and-seed`
862	- Distinguish between acceptable provisionality and sloppy unresolved ambiguity
863	- In reviews mode, fail plans that omit a must-address review concern without plan coverage or an explicit rebuttal on the merits
864	- In reviews mode, fail plans that dismiss a lone high-signal criticism only because it lacks consensus support
865	- In reviews mode, fail plans that leave materially stronger available moves or later-audit risks untouched without an explicit rationale for why they are safe to defer now
866	
867	**Project instructions:** Read ./AGENTS.md if exists — verify plans honor project guidelines
868	**Project skills/runtime:** Check repo-local `.codex/skills/` and relevant repo-local workflow/reference surfaces under `.codex/get-shit-done/`. Do not rely on `.claude/skills/` or `.agents/skills/` as governing truth for this repo.
869	</verification_context>
870	
871	<expected_output>
872	- ## VERIFICATION PASSED — all checks pass
873	- ## ISSUES FOUND — structured issue list
874	</expected_output>
875	```
876	
877	```
878	Task(
879	  prompt=checker_prompt,
880	  subagent_type="gsd-plan-checker",
881	  model="{checker_model}",
882	  description="Verify Phase {phase} plans"
883	)
884	```
885	
886	## 11. Handle Checker Return
887	
888	- **`## VERIFICATION PASSED`:** Display confirmation, proceed to step 13.
889	- **`## ISSUES FOUND`:** Display issues, check iteration count, proceed to step 12.
890	
891	**Thinking partner for architectural tradeoffs (conditional):**
892	If `features.thinking_partner` is enabled, scan the checker's issues for architectural tradeoff keywords
893	("architecture", "approach", "strategy", "pattern", "vs", "alternative"). If found:
894	
895	```
896	The plan-checker flagged an architectural decision point:
897	{issue description}
898	
899	Brief analysis:
900	- Option A: {approach_from_plan} — {pros/cons}
901	- Option B: {alternative_approach} — {pros/cons}
902	- Recommendation: {choice} aligned with {phase_goal}
903	
904	Apply this to the revision? [Yes] / [No, I'll decide]
905	```
906	
907	If yes: include the recommendation in the revision prompt. If no: proceed to revision loop as normal.
908	If thinking_partner disabled: skip this block entirely.
909	
910	## 12. Revision Loop (Max 3 Iterations)
911	
912	Track `iteration_count` (starts at 1 after initial plan + check).
913	Track `prev_issue_count` (initialized to `Infinity` before the loop begins).
914	Track `stall_reentry_count` (starts at 0; incremented each time "Adjust approach" re-enters step 8).
915	
916	**If iteration_count < 3:**
917	
918	Parse issue count from checker return: count BLOCKER + WARNING entries in the YAML issues block (structured output from gsd-plan-checker). If the checker's return contains no YAML issues block (i.e., the plan was approved with no issues), treat `issue_count` as 0 and skip the stall check — the plan passed. Proceed to step 13.
919	
920	Display: `Revision iteration {N}/3 -- {blocker_count} blockers, {warning_count} warnings`
921	
922	**Stall detection:** If `issue_count >= prev_issue_count`:
923	  Display: `Revision loop stalled — issue count not decreasing ({issue_count} issues remain after {N} iterations)`
924	
925	  **If `stall_reentry_count < 2`:**
926	    Ask user:
927	      Question: "Issues remain after {N} revision attempts with no progress. Proceed with current output?"
928	      Options: "Proceed anyway" | "Adjust approach"
929	    If "Proceed anyway": accept current plans and continue to step 13.
930	    If "Adjust approach": increment `stall_reentry_count`, open freeform discussion, then re-enter step 8 (full replanning). Note: re-entry resets `iteration_count` and `prev_issue_count` but `stall_reentry_count` persists across re-entries and is capped at 2.
931	
932	  **If `stall_reentry_count >= 2`:**
933	    Display: `Stall persists after 2 re-planning attempts. The following issues could not be resolved automatically:`
934	    List the remaining issues from the checker.
935	    Suggest: "Consider resolving these issues manually or running `/gsd-debug` to investigate root causes."
936	    Options: "Proceed anyway" | "Abandon"
937	    If "Proceed anyway": accept current plans and continue to step 13.
938	    If "Abandon": stop workflow.
939	
940	Set `prev_issue_count = issue_count`.
941	
942	Revision prompt:
943	
944	```markdown
945	<revision_context>
946	**Phase:** {phase_number}
947	**Mode:** revision
948	
949	<files_to_read>
950	- {PHASE_DIR}/*-PLAN.md (Existing plans)
951	- {context_path} (Phase steering brief from /gsd-discuss-phase)
952	- {reviews_path} (Cross-AI Review Feedback — if --reviews)
953	- __PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/references/planner-reviews.md (Review-consumer contract — if --reviews)
954	</files_to_read>
955	
956	${AGENT_SKILLS_PLANNER}
957	
958	**Checker issues:** {structured_issues_from_checker}
959	</revision_context>
960	
961	<instructions>
962	Make targeted updates to address checker issues.
963	Do NOT replan from scratch unless issues are fundamental.
964	If `--reviews` is active, preserve or improve must-address review coverage; do not drop a lone high-signal criticism or later-audit risk just because the checker focused elsewhere.
965	Return what changed.
966	</instructions>
967	```
968	
969	```
970	Task(
971	  prompt=revision_prompt,
972	  subagent_type="gsd-planner",
973	  model="{planner_model}",
974	  description="Revise Phase {phase} plans"
975	)
976	```
977	
978	After planner returns -> spawn checker again (step 10), increment iteration_count.
979	
980	**If iteration_count >= 3:**
981	
982	Display: `Max iterations reached. {N} issues remain:` + issue list
983	
984	Offer: 1) Force proceed, 2) Provide guidance and retry, 3) Abandon
985	
986	## 13. Requirements Coverage Gate
987	
988	After plans pass the checker (or checker is skipped), verify that all phase requirements are covered by at least one plan.
989	
990	**Skip if:** `phase_req_ids` is null or TBD (no requirements mapped to this phase).
991	
992	**Step 1: Extract requirement IDs claimed by plans**
993	```bash
994	# Collect all requirement IDs from plan frontmatter
995	PLAN_REQS=$(grep -h "requirements_addressed\|requirements:" ${PHASE_DIR}/*-PLAN.md 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[]' | tr ',' '\n' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//' | sort -u)
996	```
997	
998	**Step 2: Compare against phase requirements from ROADMAP**
999	
1000	For each REQ-ID in `phase_req_ids`:
1001	- If REQ-ID appears in `PLAN_REQS` → covered ✓
1002	- If REQ-ID does NOT appear in any plan → uncovered ✗
1003	
1004	**Step 3: Check CONTEXT.md features against plan objectives**
1005	
1006	Read CONTEXT.md `<decisions>` section. Extract feature/capability names. Check each against plan `<objective>` blocks. Features not mentioned in any plan objective → potentially dropped.
1007	
1008	**Step 4: Report**
1009	
1010	If all requirements covered and no dropped features:
1011	```
1012	✓ Requirements coverage: {N}/{N} REQ-IDs covered by plans
1013	```
1014	→ Proceed to step 14.
1015	
1016	If gaps found:
1017	```
1018	## ⚠ Requirements Coverage Gap
1019	
1020	{M} of {N} phase requirements are not assigned to any plan:
1021	
1022	| REQ-ID | Description | Plans |
1023	|--------|-------------|-------|
1024	| {id} | {from REQUIREMENTS.md} | None |
1025	
1026	{K} CONTEXT.md features not found in plan objectives:
1027	- {feature_name} — described in CONTEXT.md but no plan covers it
1028	
1029	Options:
1030	1. Re-plan to include missing requirements (recommended)
1031	2. Move uncovered requirements to next phase
1032	3. Proceed anyway — accept coverage gaps
1033	```
1034	
1035	If `TEXT_MODE` is true, present as a plain-text numbered list (options already shown in the block above). Otherwise use AskUserQuestion to present the options.
1036	
1037	## 13b. Record Planning Completion in STATE.md
1038	
1039	After plans pass all gates, record that planning is complete so STATE.md reflects the new phase status:
1040	
1041	```bash
1042	node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" state planned-phase --phase "${PHASE_NUMBER}" --name "${PHASE_NAME}" --plans "${PLAN_COUNT}"
1043	```
1044	
1045	This updates STATUS to "Ready to execute", sets the correct plan count, and timestamps Last Activity.
1046	
1047	## 14. Present Final Status
1048	
1049	Route to `<offer_next>` OR `auto_advance` depending on flags/config.
1050	
1051	## 15. Auto-Advance Check
1052	
1053	Check for auto-advance trigger:
1054	
1055	1. Parse `--auto` and `--chain` flags from {{GSD_ARGS}}
1056	2. **Sync chain flag with intent** — if user invoked manually (no `--auto` and no `--chain`), clear the ephemeral chain flag from any previous interrupted `--auto` chain. This does NOT touch `workflow.auto_advance` (the user's persistent settings preference):
1057	   ```bash
1058	   if [[ ! "{{GSD_ARGS}}" =~ --auto ]] && [[ ! "{{GSD_ARGS}}" =~ --chain ]]; then
1059	     node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" config-set workflow._auto_chain_active false 2>/dev/null
1060	   fi
1061	   ```
1062	3. Read both the chain flag and user preference:
1063	   ```bash
1064	   AUTO_CHAIN=$(node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" config-get workflow._auto_chain_active 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
1065	   AUTO_CFG=$(node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" config-get workflow.auto_advance 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
1066	   ```
1067	
1068	**If `--auto` or `--chain` flag present AND `AUTO_CHAIN` is not true:** Persist chain flag to config (handles direct invocation without prior discuss-phase):
1069	```bash
1070	if ([[ "{{GSD_ARGS}}" =~ --auto ]] || [[ "{{GSD_ARGS}}" =~ --chain ]]) && [[ "$AUTO_CHAIN" != "true" ]]; then
1071	  node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" config-set workflow._auto_chain_active true
1072	fi
1073	```
1074	
1075	**If `--auto` or `--chain` flag present OR `AUTO_CHAIN` is true OR `AUTO_CFG` is true:**
1076	
1077	Display banner:
1078	```
1079	━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1080	 GSD ► AUTO-ADVANCING TO EXECUTE
1081	━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1082	
1083	Plans ready. Launching execute-phase...
1084	```
1085	
1086	Launch execute-phase using the Skill tool to avoid nested Task sessions (which cause runtime freezes due to deep agent nesting):
1087	```
1088	Skill(skill="gsd-execute-phase", args="${PHASE} --auto --no-transition ${GSD_WS}")
1089	```
1090	
1091	The `--no-transition` flag tells execute-phase to return status after verification instead of chaining further. This keeps the auto-advance chain flat — each phase runs at the same nesting level rather than spawning deeper Task agents.
1092	
1093	**Handle execute-phase return:**
1094	- **PHASE COMPLETE** → Display final summary:
1095	  ```
1096	  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1097	   GSD ► PHASE ${PHASE} COMPLETE ✓
1098	  ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1099	
1100	  Auto-advance pipeline finished.
1101	
1102	  Next: /gsd-discuss-phase ${NEXT_PHASE} --auto ${GSD_WS}
1103	  ```
1104	- **GAPS FOUND / VERIFICATION FAILED** → Display result, stop chain:
1105	  ```
1106	  Auto-advance stopped: Execution needs review.
1107	
1108	  Review the output above and continue manually:
1109	  /gsd-execute-phase ${PHASE} ${GSD_WS}
1110	  ```
1111	
1112	**If neither `--auto` nor config enabled:**
1113	Route to `<offer_next>` (existing behavior).
1114	
1115	</process>
1116	
1117	<offer_next>
1118	Output this markdown directly (not as a code block):
1119	
1120	━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1121	 GSD ► PHASE {X} PLANNED ✓
1122	━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1123	
1124	**Phase {X}: {Name}** — {N} plan(s) in {M} wave(s)
1125	
1126	| Wave | Plans | What it builds |
1127	|------|-------|----------------|
1128	| 1    | 01, 02 | [objectives] |
1129	| 2    | 03     | [objective]  |
1130	
1131	Research: {Completed | Used existing | Skipped}
1132	Verification: {Passed | Passed with override | Skipped}
1133	
1134	───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1135	
1136	## ▶ Next Up
1137	
1138	**Execute Phase {X}** — run all {N} plans
1139	
1140	/clear then:
1141	
1142	/gsd-execute-phase {X} ${GSD_WS}
1143	
1144	───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1145	
1146	**Also available:**
1147	- cat .planning/phases/{phase-dir}/*-PLAN.md — review plans
1148	- /gsd-plan-phase {X} --research — re-research first
1149	- /gsd-review --phase {X} --all — peer review plans with external AIs
1150	- /gsd-plan-phase {X} --reviews — replan incorporating review feedback
1151	
1152	───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1153	</offer_next>
1154	
1155	<windows_troubleshooting>
1156	**Windows users:** If plan-phase freezes during agent spawning (common on Windows due to
1157	stdio deadlocks with MCP servers — see Claude Code issue anthropics/claude-code#28126):
1158	
1159	1. **Force-kill:** Close the terminal (Ctrl+C may not work)
1160	2. **Clean up orphaned processes:**
1161	   ```powershell
1162	   # Kill orphaned node processes from stale MCP servers
1163	   Get-Process node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {$_.StartTime -lt (Get-Date).AddHours(-1)} | Stop-Process -Force
1164	   ```
1165	3. **Clean up stale task directories:**
1166	   ```powershell
1167	   # Remove stale subagent task dirs (Claude Code never cleans these on crash)
1168	   Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\tasks\*" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1169	   ```
1170	4. **Reduce MCP server count:** Temporarily disable non-essential MCP servers in settings.json
1171	5. **Retry:** Restart Claude Code and run `/gsd-plan-phase` again
1172	
1173	If freezes persist, try `--skip-research` to reduce the agent chain from 3 to 2 agents:
1174	```
1175	/gsd-plan-phase N --skip-research
1176	```
1177	</windows_troubleshooting>
1178	
1179	<success_criteria>
1180	- [ ] .planning/ directory validated
1181	- [ ] Phase validated against roadmap
1182	- [ ] Phase directory created if needed
1183	- [ ] CONTEXT.md loaded early (step 4) and passed to ALL agents
1184	- [ ] Research completed (unless --skip-research or --gaps or exists)
1185	- [ ] gsd-phase-researcher spawned with CONTEXT.md
1186	- [ ] Existing plans checked
1187	- [ ] gsd-planner spawned with CONTEXT.md + RESEARCH.md
1188	- [ ] Plans created (PLANNING COMPLETE or CHECKPOINT handled)
1189	- [ ] gsd-plan-checker spawned with CONTEXT.md
1190	- [ ] Verification passed OR user override OR max iterations with user decision
1191	- [ ] User sees status between agent spawns
1192	- [ ] User knows next steps
1193	</success_criteria>

file.content:
<purpose>
Create executable phase prompts (PLAN.md files) for a roadmap phase with integrated research and verification. Default flow: Research (if needed) -> Plan -> Verify -> Done. Orchestrates gsd-phase-researcher, gsd-planner, and gsd-plan-checker agents with a revision loop (max 3 iterations).
</purpose>

<required_reading>
Read all files referenced by the invoking prompt's execution_context before starting.

@__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/references/ui-brand.md
@__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/references/revision-loop.md
@__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/references/gate-prompts.md
@__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/references/agent-contracts.md
@__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/references/gates.md
@__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/references/planner-reviews.md
</required_reading>

<available_agent_types>
Valid GSD subagent types (use exact names — do not fall back to 'general-purpose'):
- gsd-phase-researcher — Researches technical approaches for a phase
- gsd-planner — Creates detailed plans from phase scope
- gsd-plan-checker — Reviews plan quality before execution
</available_agent_types>

<process>

## 1. Initialize

Load all context in one call (paths only to minimize orchestrator context):

```bash
INIT=$(node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" init plan-phase "$PHASE")
if [[ "$INIT" == @file:* ]]; then INIT=$(cat "${INIT#@file:}"); fi
AGENT_SKILLS_RESEARCHER=$(node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" agent-skills gsd-researcher 2>/dev/null)
AGENT_SKILLS_PLANNER=$(node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" agent-skills gsd-planner 2>/dev/null)
AGENT_SKILLS_CHECKER=$(node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" agent-skills gsd-checker 2>/dev/null)
CONTEXT_WINDOW=$(node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" config-get context_window 2>/dev/null || echo "200000")
```

When `CONTEXT_WINDOW >= 500000`, the planner prompt includes prior phase CONTEXT.md files so cross-phase decisions are consistent (e.g., "use library X for all data fetching" from Phase 2 is visible to Phase 5's planner).

Parse JSON for: `researcher_model`, `planner_model`, `checker_model`, `research_enabled`, `plan_checker_enabled`, `nyquist_validation_enabled`, `commit_docs`, `text_mode`, `phase_found`, `phase_dir`, `phase_number`, `phase_name`, `phase_slug`, `padded_phase`, `has_research`, `has_context`, `has_reviews`, `has_plans`, `plan_count`, `planning_exists`, `roadmap_exists`, `phase_req_ids`, `response_language`.

**If `response_language` is set:** Include `response_language: {value}` in all spawned subagent prompts so any user-facing output stays in the configured language.

**File paths (for <files_to_read> blocks):** `state_path`, `roadmap_path`, `requirements_path`, `context_path`, `research_path`, `verification_path`, `uat_path`, `reviews_path`. These are null if files don't exist.

**If `planning_exists` is false:** Error — run `/gsd-new-project` first.

## 2. Parse and Normalize Arguments

Extract from {{GSD_ARGS}}: phase number (integer or decimal like `2.1`), flags (`--research`, `--skip-research`, `--gaps`, `--skip-verify`, `--prd <filepath>`, `--reviews`, `--text`, `--allow-no-context`).

## 5.7. Schema Push Detection Gate

> Detects schema-relevant files in the phase scope and injects a mandatory `[BLOCKING]` schema push task into the plan. Prevents false-positive verification where build/types pass because TypeScript types come from config, not the live database.

Check if any files in the phase scope match schema patterns:

```bash
PHASE_SECTION=$(node "__PROJECT_ROOT__/.codex/get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs" roadmap get-phase "${PHASE}" --pick section 2>/dev/null)
```

Scan `PHASE_SECTION`, `CONTEXT.md` (if loaded), and `RESEARCH.md` (if exists) for file paths matching these ORM patterns:

| ORM | File Patterns |
|-----|--------------|
| Payload CMS | `src/collections/**/*.ts`, `src/globals/**/*.ts` |
| Prisma | `prisma/schema.prisma`, `prisma/schema/*.prisma` |
| Drizzle | `drizzle/schema.ts`, `src/db/schema.ts`, `drizzle/*.ts` |
| Supabase | `supabase/migrations/*.sql` |
| TypeORM | `src/entities/**/*.ts`, `src/migrations/**/*.ts` |

Also check if any existing PLAN.md files for this phase already reference these file patterns in `files_modified`.

**If schema-relevant files detected:**

Set `SCHEMA_PUSH_REQUIRED=true` and `SCHEMA_ORM={detected_orm}`.

Determine the push command for the detected ORM:

| ORM | Push Command | Non-TTY Workaround |
|-----|-------------|-------------------|
| Payload CMS | `npx payload migrate` | `CI=true PAYLOAD_MIGRATING=true npx payload migrate` |
| Prisma | `npx prisma db push` | `npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss` (if destructive) |
| Drizzle | `npx drizzle-kit push` | `npx drizzle-kit push` |
| Supabase | `supabase db push` | Set `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` env var |
| TypeORM | `npx typeorm migration:run` | `npx typeorm migration:run -d src/data-source.ts` |

Inject the following into the planner prompt (step 8) as an additional constraint:

```markdown
<schema_push_requirement>
**[BLOCKING] Schema Push Required**

This phase modifies schema-relevant files ({detected_files}). The planner MUST include
a `[BLOCKING]` task that runs the database schema push command AFTER all schema file
modifications are complete but BEFORE verification.

- ORM detected: {SCHEMA_ORM}
- Push command: {push_command}
- Non-TTY workaround: {env_hint}
- If push requires interactive prompts that cannot be suppressed, flag the task for
  manual intervention with `autonomous: false`

This task is mandatory — the phase CANNOT pass verification without it. Build and
type checks will pass without the push (types come from config, not the live database),
creating a false-positive verification state.
</schema_push_requirement>
```

Display: `Schema files detected ({SCHEMA_ORM}) — [BLOCKING] push task will be injected into plans`

**If no schema-relevant files detected:** Skip silently to step 6.

```markdown
<deep_work_rules>
## Anti-Shallow Execution Rules (MANDATORY)

Every task MUST include these fields — they are NOT optional:

1. **`<read_first>`** — Files the executor MUST read before touching anything. Always include:
   - The file being modified (so executor sees current state, not assumptions)
   - Any "source of truth" file referenced in CONTEXT.md (reference implementations, existing patterns, config files, schemas)
   - Any file whose patterns, signatures, types, or conventions must be replicated or respected

2. **`<acceptance_criteria>`** — Verifiable conditions that prove the task was done correctly. Rules:
   - Every criterion must be checkable with grep, file read, test command, or CLI output
   - NEVER use subjective language ("looks correct", "properly configured", "consistent with")
   - ALWAYS include exact strings, patterns, values, or command outputs that must be present
   - Examples:
     - Code: `auth.py contains def verify_token(` / `test_auth.py exits 0`
     - Config: `.env.example contains DATABASE_URL=` / `Dockerfile contains HEALTHCHECK`
     - Docs: `README.md contains '## Installation'` / `API.md lists all endpoints`
     - Infra: `deploy.yml has rollback step` / `docker-compose.yml has healthcheck for db`

3. **`<action>`** — Must include CONCRETE values, not references. Rules:
   - NEVER say "align X with Y", "match X to Y", "update to be consistent" without specifying the exact target state
   - ALWAYS include the actual values: config keys, function signatures, SQL statements, class names, import paths, env vars, etc.
   - If CONTEXT.md has a comparison table or expected values, copy them into the action verbatim
   - The executor should be able to complete the task from the action text alone, without needing to read CONTEXT.md or reference files (read_first is for verification, not discovery)

**Why this matters:** Executor agents work from the plan text. Vague instructions like "update the config to match production" produce shallow one-line changes. Concrete instructions like "add DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... , set POOL_SIZE=20, add REDIS_URL=redis://..." produce complete work. The cost of verbose plans is far less than the cost of re-doing shallow execution.
</deep_work_rules>
```

## 9. Handle Planner Return

- **`## PLANNING COMPLETE`:** Display plan count. If `--reviews` is active, do not accept this state unless the planner return includes `### Review Feedback Addressed`. If must-address concerns were deferred or rejected, the return must also include the corresponding tables with reasons on the merits. If `--skip-verify` or `plan_checker_enabled` is false (from init): skip to step 13. Otherwise: step 10.
- **`## PHASE SPLIT RECOMMENDED`:** The planner determined the phase is too complex to implement all user decisions without simplifying them. Handle in step 9b.
- **`## CHECKPOINT REACHED`:** Present to user, get response, spawn continuation (step 12)
- **`## PLANNING INCONCLUSIVE`:** Show attempts, offer: Add context / Retry / Manual

## 9b. Handle Phase Split Recommendation

When the planner returns `## PHASE SPLIT RECOMMENDED`, it means the phase has too many decisions to implement at full fidelity within the plan budget. The planner proposes groupings.

**Extract from planner return:**
- Proposed sub-phases (e.g., "17a: processing core (D-01 to D-19)", "17b: billing + config UX (D-20 to D-27)")
- Which D-XX decisions go in each sub-phase
- Why the split is necessary (decision count, complexity estimate)

**Present to user:**
```
## Phase {X} is too complex for full-fidelity implementation

The planner found {N} decisions that cannot all be implemented without
simplifying some. Instead of reducing your decisions, we recommend splitting:

**Option 1: Split into sub-phases**
- Phase {X}a: {name} — {D-XX to D-YY} ({N} decisions)
- Phase {X}b: {name} — {D-XX to D-YY} ({M} decisions)

**Option 2: Proceed anyway** (planner will attempt all, quality may degrade)

**Option 3: Prioritize** — you choose which decisions to implement now,
rest become a follow-up phase
```

Use AskUserQuestion with these 3 options.

**If "Split":** Use `/gsd-insert-phase` to create the sub-phases, then replan each.
**If "Proceed":** Return to planner with instruction to attempt all decisions at full fidelity, accepting more plans/tasks.
**If "Prioritize":** Use AskUserQuestion (multiSelect) to let user pick which D-XX are "now" vs "later". Create CONTEXT.md for each sub-phase with the selected decisions.

## 12. Revision Loop (Max 3 Iterations)

Track `iteration_count` (starts at 1 after initial plan + check).
Track `prev_issue_count` (initialized to `Infinity` before the loop begins).
Track `stall_reentry_count` (starts at 0; incremented each time "Adjust approach" re-enters step 8).

**If iteration_count < 3:**

Parse issue count from checker return: count BLOCKER + WARNING entries in the YAML issues block (structured output from gsd-plan-checker). If the checker's return contains no YAML issues block (i.e., the plan was approved with no issues), treat `issue_count` as 0 and skip the stall check — the plan passed. Proceed to step 13.

Display: `Revision iteration {N}/3 -- {blocker_count} blockers, {warning_count} warnings`

**Stall detection:** If `issue_count >= prev_issue_count`:
  Display: `Revision loop stalled — issue count not decreasing ({issue_count} issues remain after {N} iterations)`

  **If `stall_reentry_count < 2`:**
    Ask user:
      Question: "Issues remain after {N} revision attempts with no progress. Proceed with current output?"
      Options: "Proceed anyway" | "Adjust approach"
    If "Proceed anyway": accept current plans and continue to step 13.
    If "Adjust approach": increment `stall_reentry_count`, open freeform discussion, then re-enter step 8 (full replanning). Note: re-entry resets `iteration_count` and `prev_issue_count` but `stall_reentry_count` persists across re-entries and is capped at 2.

  **If `stall_reentry_count >= 2`:**
    Display: `Stall persists after 2 re-planning attempts. The following issues could not be resolved automatically:`
    List the remaining issues from the checker.
    Suggest: "Consider resolving these issues manually or running `/gsd-debug` to investigate root causes."
    Options: "Proceed anyway" | "Abandon"
    If "Proceed anyway": accept current plans and continue to step 13.
    If "Abandon": stop workflow.

Set `prev_issue_count = issue_count`.

**Windows users:** If plan-phase freezes during agent spawning (common on Windows due to
stdio deadlocks with MCP servers — see Claude Code issue anthropics/claude-code#28126):

1. **Force-kill:** Close the terminal (Ctrl+C may not work)
2. **Clean up orphaned processes:**
   ```powershell
   # Kill orphaned node processes from stale MCP servers
   Get-Process node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {$_.StartTime -lt (Get-Date).AddHours(-1)} | Stop-Process -Force
   ```
3. **Clean up stale task directories:**
   ```powershell
   # Remove stale subagent task dirs (Claude Code never cleans these on crash)
   Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\tasks\*" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
   ```
4. **Reduce MCP server count:** Temporarily disable non-essential MCP servers in settings.json
5. **Retry:** Restart Claude Code and run `/gsd-plan-phase` again

If freezes persist, try `--skip-research` to reduce the agent chain from 3 to 2 agents:
```
/gsd-plan-phase N --skip-research
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	
3	"""Run a Claude headless probe and print a compact diagnostic summary.
4	
5	Operational note:
6	If the prompt tells Claude to read a repo-local spec or wrapper file, prefer
7	that file to live in the repo (not `/tmp`) and usually pass
8	`--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Without that, headless probes can fail in a
9	misleading way: startup/auth complete, `/v1/messages` is sent, then the run dies
10	before any assistant/result event is emitted.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import argparse
16	import collections
17	import json
18	import subprocess
19	import sys
20	import tempfile
21	import time
22	from pathlib import Path
23	
24	
25	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
26	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
27	        description="Run a Claude headless probe with stream-json diagnostics."
28	    )
29	    parser.add_argument("--label", required=True, help="Short label for temp artifact names.")
30	    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True, help="Claude model string, e.g. sonnet or opus[1m].")
31	    parser.add_argument("--effort", default="medium", help="Reasoning effort.")
32	    prompt_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
33	    prompt_group.add_argument("--prompt", help="Inline prompt text.")
34	    prompt_group.add_argument(
35	        "--prompt-file",
36	        help=(
37	            "Path to a prompt file. If the prompt instructs Claude to read other "
38	            "repo files, prefer a repo-local path and usually pair this with "
39	            "--dangerously-skip-permissions."
40	        ),
41	    )
42	    parser.add_argument(
43	        "--output-dir",
44	        default="/tmp",
45	        help="Directory for stream/stderr/debug artifacts. Default: /tmp",
46	    )
47	    parser.add_argument(
48	        "--dangerously-skip-permissions",
49	        action="store_true",
50	        help=(
51	            "Pass --dangerously-skip-permissions to Claude for the probe. "
52	            "Recommended when the prompt asks Claude to read repo-local spec or "
53	            "wrapper files."
54	        ),
55	    )
56	    return parser.parse_args()
57	
58	
59	def load_prompt(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
60	    if args.prompt is not None:
61	        return args.prompt
62	    return Path(args.prompt_file).read_text()
63	
64	
65	def extract_blocks(obj: dict) -> list[str]:
66	    blocks: list[str] = []
67	    if obj.get("type") == "assistant":
68	        message = obj.get("message") or {}
69	        for item in message.get("content", []) or []:
70	            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("type") == "text" and item.get("text"):
71	                blocks.append(item["text"])
72	    if obj.get("type") == "result":
73	        result = obj.get("result")
74	        if isinstance(result, str) and result:
75	            blocks.append(result)
76	    return blocks
77	
78	
79	def summarize_stream(path: Path) -> dict:
80	    event_counts: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
81	    system_subtypes: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
82	    extracted: list[str] = []
83	    last_error_like: str | None = None
84	
85	    if not path.exists():
86	        return {
87	            "event_counts": {},
88	            "system_subtypes": {},
89	            "text_chunks": 0,
90	            "last_text": None,
91	            "last_error_like": None,
92	        }
93	
94	    with path.open() as handle:
95	        for raw_line in handle:
96	            raw_line = raw_line.strip()
97	            if not raw_line:
98	                continue
99	            try:
100	                obj = json.loads(raw_line)
101	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
102	                continue
103	            event_type = obj.get("type")
104	            if event_type:
105	                event_counts[event_type] += 1
106	            if event_type == "system" and obj.get("subtype"):
107	                system_subtypes[obj["subtype"]] += 1
108	            extracted.extend(extract_blocks(obj))
109	            if "error" in raw_line.lower() or "failed" in raw_line.lower():
110	                last_error_like = raw_line
111	
112	    return {
113	        "event_counts": dict(event_counts),
114	        "system_subtypes": dict(system_subtypes),
115	        "text_chunks": len(extracted),
116	        "last_text": extracted[-1] if extracted else None,
117	        "last_error_like": last_error_like,
118	    }
119	
120	
121	def tail_text(path: Path, lines: int = 20) -> str:
122	    if not path.exists():
123	        return ""
124	    data = path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
125	    return "\n".join(data[-lines:])
126	
127	
128	def main() -> int:
129	    args = parse_args()
130	    prompt = load_prompt(args)
131	    output_dir = Path(args.output_dir)
132	    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""Run a Claude headless probe and print a compact diagnostic summary.

Operational note:
If the prompt tells Claude to read a repo-local spec or wrapper file, prefer
that file to live in the repo (not `/tmp`) and usually pass
`--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Without that, headless probes can fail in a
misleading way: startup/auth complete, `/v1/messages` is sent, then the run dies
before any assistant/result event is emitted.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import collections
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Run a Claude headless probe with stream-json diagnostics."
    )
    parser.add_argument("--label", required=True, help="Short label for temp artifact names.")
    parser.add_argument("--model", required=True, help="Claude model string, e.g. sonnet or opus[1m].")
    parser.add_argument("--effort", default="medium", help="Reasoning effort.")
    prompt_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    prompt_group.add_argument("--prompt", help="Inline prompt text.")
    prompt_group.add_argument(
        "--prompt-file",
        help=(
            "Path to a prompt file. If the prompt instructs Claude to read other "
            "repo files, prefer a repo-local path and usually pair this with "
            "--dangerously-skip-permissions."
        ),
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-dir",
        default="/tmp",
        help="Directory for stream/stderr/debug artifacts. Default: /tmp",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dangerously-skip-permissions",
        action="store_true",
        help=(
            "Pass --dangerously-skip-permissions to Claude for the probe. "
            "Recommended when the prompt asks Claude to read repo-local spec or "
            "wrapper files."
        ),
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


def load_prompt(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    if args.prompt is not None:
        return args.prompt
    return Path(args.prompt_file).read_text()


def extract_blocks(obj: dict) -> list[str]:
    blocks: list[str] = []
    if obj.get("type") == "assistant":
        message = obj.get("message") or {}
        for item in message.get("content", []) or []:
            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("type") == "text" and item.get("text"):
                blocks.append(item["text"])
    if obj.get("type") == "result":
        result = obj.get("result")
        if isinstance(result, str) and result:
            blocks.append(result)
    return blocks


def summarize_stream(path: Path) -> dict:
    event_counts: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    system_subtypes: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    extracted: list[str] = []
    last_error_like: str | None = None

    if not path.exists():
        return {
            "event_counts": {},
            "system_subtypes": {},
            "text_chunks": 0,
            "last_text": None,
            "last_error_like": None,
        }

    with path.open() as handle:
        for raw_line in handle:
            raw_line = raw_line.strip()
            if not raw_line:
                continue
            try:
                obj = json.loads(raw_line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            event_type = obj.get("type")
            if event_type:
                event_counts[event_type] += 1
            if event_type == "system" and obj.get("subtype"):
                system_subtypes[obj["subtype"]] += 1
            extracted.extend(extract_blocks(obj))
            if "error" in raw_line.lower() or "failed" in raw_line.lower():
                last_error_like = raw_line

    return {
        "event_counts": dict(event_counts),
        "system_subtypes": dict(system_subtypes),
        "text_chunks": len(extracted),
        "last_text": extracted[-1] if extracted else None,
        "last_error_like": last_error_like,
    }


def tail_text(path: Path, lines: int = 20) -> str:
    if not path.exists():
        return ""
    data = path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
    return "\n".join(data[-lines:])


def main() -> int:
    args = parse_args()
    prompt = load_prompt(args)
    output_dir = Path(args.output_dir)
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    stamp = time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    prefix = f"{args.label}-{stamp}"
    stream_file = Path(tempfile.mktemp(prefix=prefix + ".", suffix=".stream.jsonl", dir=output_dir))
    stderr_file = Path(tempfile.mktemp(prefix=prefix + ".", suffix=".stderr.log", dir=output_dir))
    debug_file = Path(tempfile.mktemp(prefix=prefix + ".", suffix=".debug.log", dir=output_dir))

    cmd = [
        "claude",
        "-p",
        "--model",
        args.model,
        "--effort",
        args.effort,
        "--output-format",
        "stream-json",
        "--include-partial-messages",
        "--verbose",
        "--debug-file",
        str(debug_file),
        prompt,
    ]

    if args.dangerously_skip_permissions:
        cmd.insert(2, "--dangerously-skip-permissions")

    start = time.time()
    with stream_file.open("w") as stream_handle, stderr_file.open("w") as stderr_handle:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            cmd,
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stdout=stream_handle,
            stderr=stderr_handle,
            text=True,
            check=False,
        )
    elapsed = time.time() - start

    summary = summarize_stream(stream_file)
    stderr_tail = tail_text(stderr_file, lines=10)
    debug_tail = tail_text(debug_file, lines=10)

    print(f"label={args.label}")
    print(f"exit_code={completed.returncode}")
    print(f"elapsed_seconds={elapsed:.3f}")
    print(f"stream={stream_file}")
    print(f"stderr={stderr_file}")
    print(f"debug={debug_file}")
    print(f"stream_bytes={stream_file.stat().st_size if stream_file.exists() else 0}")
    print(f"stderr_bytes={stderr_file.stat().st_size if stderr_file.exists() else 0}")
    print(f"debug_bytes={debug_file.stat().st_size if debug_file.exists() else 0}")
    print(f"event_counts={json.dumps(summary['event_counts'], sort_keys=True)}")
    print(f"system_subtypes={json.dumps(summary['system_subtypes'], sort_keys=True)}")
    print(f"text_chunks={summary['text_chunks']}")
    if summary["last_text"]:
        print("last_text_begin")
        print(summary["last_text"].rstrip())
        print("last_text_end")
    if summary["last_error_like"]:
        print("last_error_like_begin")
        print(summary["last_error_like"])
        print("last_error_like_end")
    if stderr_tail:
        print("stderr_tail_begin")
        print(stderr_tail)
        print("stderr_tail_end")
    if debug_tail:
        print("debug_tail_begin")
        print(debug_tail)
        print("debug_tail_end")

    return completed.returncode


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	
3	"""Extract text-bearing content from Claude/Codex stream-json logs.
4	
5	Examples:
6	  python3 tooling/codex/extract_stream_text.py run.stream.jsonl
7	  python3 tooling/codex/extract_stream_text.py run.stream.jsonl --tail 100
8	  python3 tooling/codex/extract_stream_text.py run.stream.jsonl --head 50
9	  python3 tooling/codex/extract_stream_text.py run.stream.jsonl --range 120:180
10	  python3 tooling/codex/extract_stream_text.py run.stream.jsonl --last-message
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import argparse
16	import json
17	import sys
18	from collections import deque
19	from pathlib import Path
20	from typing import Iterable
21	
22	
23	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
24	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
25	        description="Extract text-bearing content from a Claude/Codex stream-json log."
26	    )
27	    parser.add_argument("path", help="Path to the stream-jsonl file.")
28	
29	    mode = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
30	    mode.add_argument("--head", type=int, help="Use only the first N raw jsonl lines.")
31	    mode.add_argument("--tail", type=int, help="Use only the last N raw jsonl lines.")
32	    mode.add_argument(
33	        "--range",
34	        dest="line_range",
35	        help="Use only raw jsonl lines START:END (1-based, inclusive).",
36	    )
37	    mode.add_argument(
38	        "--last-message",
39	        action="store_true",
40	        help="Print only the last text-bearing message/result found.",
41	    )
42	
43	    parser.add_argument(
44	        "--include-result",
45	        action="store_true",
46	        help="Include result text if present.",
47	    )
48	    parser.add_argument(
49	        "--include-thinking",
50	        action="store_true",
51	        help="Include thinking/redacted_thinking content if present.",
52	    )
53	    parser.add_argument(
54	        "--show-source-lines",
55	        action="store_true",
56	        help="Prefix extracted chunks with their source jsonl line numbers.",
57	    )
58	    parser.add_argument(
59	        "--output",
60	        help="Write extracted text to this file instead of stdout.",
61	    )
62	    args = parser.parse_args()
63	
64	    if args.head is not None and args.head < 1:
65	        parser.error("--head must be at least 1")
66	    if args.tail is not None and args.tail < 1:
67	        parser.error("--tail must be at least 1")
68	    if args.line_range:
69	        parse_line_range(args.line_range)
70	
71	    return args
72	
73	
74	def parse_line_range(spec: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
75	    if ":" not in spec:
76	        raise SystemExit("--range must look like START:END")
77	    start_raw, end_raw = spec.split(":", 1)
78	    try:
79	        start = int(start_raw)
80	        end = int(end_raw)
81	    except ValueError as exc:
82	        raise SystemExit("--range bounds must be integers") from exc
83	    if start < 1 or end < start:
84	        raise SystemExit("--range must use 1-based inclusive bounds with END >= START")
85	    return start, end
86	
87	
88	def iter_selected_lines(path: Path, args: argparse.Namespace) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:
89	    if args.head is not None:
90	        selected: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
91	        with path.open() as handle:
92	            for idx, line in enumerate(handle, start=1):
93	                if idx > args.head:
94	                    break
95	                selected.append((idx, line))
96	        return selected
97	
98	    if args.tail is not None:
99	        bucket: deque[tuple[int, str]] = deque(maxlen=args.tail)
100	        with path.open() as handle:
101	            for idx, line in enumerate(handle, start=1):
102	                bucket.append((idx, line))
103	        return list(bucket)
104	
105	    if args.line_range:
106	        start, end = parse_line_range(args.line_range)
107	        selected = []
108	        with path.open() as handle:
109	            for idx, line in enumerate(handle, start=1):
110	                if idx < start:
111	                    continue
112	                if idx > end:
113	                    break
114	                selected.append((idx, line))
115	        return selected
116	
117	    with path.open() as handle:
118	        return [(idx, line) for idx, line in enumerate(handle, start=1)]
119	
120	
121	def extract_blocks(obj: dict, include_result: bool, include_thinking: bool) -> list[str]:
122	    event_type = obj.get("type")
123	    blocks: list[str] = []
124	
125	    if event_type in {"assistant", "user"}:
126	        message = obj.get("message") or {}
127	        for item in message.get("content", []) or []:
128	            if not isinstance(item, dict):
129	                continue
130	            item_type = item.get("type")
131	            if item_type == "text" and item.get("text"):
132	                blocks.append(item["text"])
133	            elif include_thinking and item_type in {"thinking", "redacted_thinking"}:
134	                text = item.get("thinking") or item.get("text")
135	                if text:
136	                    blocks.append(text)
137	
138	    if include_result and event_type == "result":
139	        result = obj.get("result")
140	        if isinstance(result, str) and result:
141	            blocks.append(result)
142	
143	    return blocks
144	
145	
146	def format_chunk(source_line: int, text: str, show_source_lines: bool) -> str:
147	    if not show_source_lines:
148	        return text.rstrip()
149	    return f"[jsonl:{source_line}]\n{text.rstrip()}"
150	
151	
152	def main() -> int:
153	    args = parse_args()
154	    path = Path(args.path)
155	    if not path.exists():
156	        raise SystemExit(f"File not found: {path}")
157	
158	    selected = iter_selected_lines(path, args)
159	    extracted: list[str] = []
160	
161	    for source_line, raw_line in selected:
162	        stripped = raw_line.strip()
163	        if not stripped:
164	            continue
165	        try:
166	            obj = json.loads(stripped)
167	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
168	            continue
169	        for block in extract_blocks(obj, args.include_result, args.include_thinking):
170	            if block.strip():
171	                extracted.append(format_chunk(source_line, block, args.show_source_lines))
172	
173	    if args.last_message:
174	        output_text = extracted[-1] if extracted else ""
175	    else:
176	        output_text = "\n\n".join(extracted)
177	
178	    if args.output:
179	        Path(args.output).write_text(output_text)
180	    else:
181	        sys.stdout.write(output_text)
182	        if output_text and not output_text.endswith("\n"):
183	            sys.stdout.write("\n")
184	
185	    return 0
186	
187	
188	if __name__ == "__main__":
189	    raise SystemExit(main())
190

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	
3	"""Capture requested-versus-effective Codex launch truth from state_5.sqlite."""
4	
5	from __future__ import annotations
6	
7	import argparse
8	import json
9	import sqlite3
10	import sys
11	from dataclasses import dataclass
12	from datetime import datetime
13	from pathlib import Path
14	from typing import Iterable
15	
16	
17	DEFAULT_DB_PATH = Path.home() / ".codex" / "state_5.sqlite"
18	KNOWN_SANDBOX_TYPES = {
19	    "danger-full-access",
20	    "read-only",
21	    "workspace-write",
22	}
23	
24	
25	@dataclass
26	class RequestedSettings:
27	    model: str | None
28	    reasoning_effort: str | None
29	    approval_mode: str | None
30	    sandbox_policy: str | None
31	    agent: str | None
32	    agent_path: str | None
33	
34	    def as_rows(self) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
35	        rows = [
36	            ("model", self.model),
37	            ("reasoning_effort", self.reasoning_effort),
38	            ("approval_mode", self.approval_mode),
39	            ("sandbox_policy", self.sandbox_policy),
40	            ("requested_agent", self.agent),
41	            ("requested_agent_path", self.agent_path),
42	        ]
43	        return [(label, value) for label, value in rows if value]
44	
45	    def has_comparison_inputs(self) -> bool:
46	        return bool(self.as_rows())
47	
48	
49	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
50	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
51	        description=(
52	            "Capture requested-versus-effective worker launch settings from "
53	            "~/.codex/state_5.sqlite into a reviewable markdown artifact."
54	        )
55	    )
56	    boundary_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
57	    boundary_group.add_argument(
58	        "--since",
59	        help=(
60	            "Capture worker threads created at or after this boundary. Accepts "
61	            "unix seconds or an ISO-8601 timestamp."
62	        ),
63	    )
64	    boundary_group.add_argument(
65	        "--latest",
66	        type=int,
67	        help=(
68	            "Capture the latest N worker threads. Use only when you did not "
69	            "record a stronger pre-spawn boundary."
70	        ),
71	    )
72	    parser.add_argument(
73	        "--label",
74	        required=True,
75	        help="Short human label for the launch being captured.",
76	    )
77	    parser.add_argument(
78	        "--db",
79	        default=str(DEFAULT_DB_PATH),
80	        help="Path to the Codex sqlite state database.",
81	    )
82	    parser.add_argument("--requested-model")
83	    parser.add_argument("--requested-reasoning")
84	    parser.add_argument("--requested-approval")
85	    parser.add_argument(
86	        "--requested-sandbox",
87	        help=(
88	            "Requested sandbox policy. Shorthand values such as "
89	            "'danger-full-access' are accepted."
90	        ),
91	    )
92	    parser.add_argument(
93	        "--requested-agent",
94	        help="Named agent or role that the operator intended to launch.",
95	    )
96	    parser.add_argument(
97	        "--requested-agent-path",
98	        help="Requested agent config path, if the launch depended on a specific file.",
99	    )
100	    parser.add_argument(
101	        "--include-non-worker",
102	        action="store_true",
103	        help="Do not filter the capture to threads whose agent_role is 'worker'.",
104	    )
105	    parser.add_argument(
106	        "--output",
107	        help="Write markdown output to this path instead of stdout.",
108	    )
109	    args = parser.parse_args()
110	    if args.latest is not None and args.latest < 1:
111	        parser.error("--latest must be at least 1")
112	    return args
113	
114	
115	def parse_boundary(value: str) -> int:
116	    stripped = value.strip()
117	    if stripped.isdigit():
118	        return int(stripped)
119	
120	    try:
121	        if stripped.endswith("Z"):
122	            stripped = stripped[:-1] + "+00:00"
123	        parsed = datetime.fromisoformat(stripped)
124	    except ValueError as exc:
125	        raise SystemExit(
126	            "--since must be unix seconds or an ISO-8601 timestamp"
127	        ) from exc
128	
129	    if parsed.tzinfo is None:
130	        parsed = parsed.astimezone()
131	
132	    return int(parsed.timestamp())
133	
134	
135	def normalize_sandbox(raw_value: str | None) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
136	    if raw_value is None:
137	        return None, None
138	
139	    value = raw_value.strip()
140	    if not value:
141	        return None, None
142	
143	    if value in KNOWN_SANDBOX_TYPES:
144	        return value, json.dumps({"type": value}, sort_keys=True)
145	
146	    try:
147	        parsed = json.loads(value)
148	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
149	        return value, value
150	
151	    if isinstance(parsed, dict) and set(parsed.keys()) == {"type"}:
152	        sandbox_type = parsed.get("type")
153	        if isinstance(sandbox_type, str):
154	            return sandbox_type, json.dumps(parsed, sort_keys=True)
155	
156	    return json.dumps(parsed, sort_keys=True), json.dumps(parsed, sort_keys=True)
157	
158	
159	def fetch_threads(
160	    db_path: Path,
161	    since: int | None,
162	    latest: int | None,
163	    include_non_worker: bool,
164	) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
165	    filters: list[str] = []
166	    parameters: list[object] = []
167	
168	    if not include_non_worker:
169	        filters.append("agent_role = 'worker'")
170	    if since is not None:
171	        filters.append("created_at >= ?")
172	        parameters.append(since)
173	
174	    where_clause = ""
175	    if filters:
176	        where_clause = "WHERE " + " AND ".join(filters)
177	
178	    query = (
179	        "SELECT id, created_at, updated_at, model, reasoning_effort, "
180	        "sandbox_policy, approval_mode, agent_role, agent_path "
181	        "FROM threads "
182	        f"{where_clause} "
183	        "ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC"
184	    )
185	
186	    if latest is not None:
187	        query += " LIMIT ?"
188	        parameters.append(latest)
189	
190	    connection = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
191	    connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
192	    try:
193	        return connection.execute(query, parameters).fetchall()
194	    finally:
195	        connection.close()
196	
197	
198	def format_local_timestamp(epoch_seconds: int | None) -> str:
199	    if epoch_seconds is None:
200	        return "-"
201	    return datetime.fromtimestamp(epoch_seconds).astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds")
202	
203	
204	def summarize_field(
205	    field_name: str,
206	    requested_display: str | None,
207	    requested_key: str | None,
208	    effective_values: Iterable[str | None],
209	) -> str:
210	    if requested_display is None or requested_key is None:
211	        return f"- `{field_name}`: not captured as a requested setting."
212	
213	    normalized_effective = [value for value in effective_values if value]
214	    if not normalized_effective:
215	        return (
216	            f"- `{field_name}`: unresolved. Requested `{requested_display}`, but no "
217	            "effective value was present in the captured thread rows."
218	        )
219	
220	    matches = sum(1 for value in normalized_effective if value == requested_key)
221	    total = len(normalized_effective)
222	
223	    if matches == total:
224	        return (
225	            f"- `{field_name}`: matched requested `{requested_display}` across "
226	            f"{matches}/{total} captured rows."
227	        )
228	
229	    return (
230	        f"- `{field_name}`: mixed or mismatched. Requested `{requested_display}`; "
231	        f"{matches}/{total} captured rows matched."
232	    )
233	
234	
235	def render_markdown(
236	    label: str,
237	    db_path: Path,
238	    boundary_description: str,
239	    requested: RequestedSettings,
240	    rows: list[sqlite3.Row],
241	) -> str:
242	    captured_at = datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds")
243	
244	    requested_sandbox_display, requested_sandbox_key = normalize_sandbox(
245	        requested.sandbox_policy
246	    )
247	
248	    model_summary = summarize_field(
249	        "model",
250	        requested.model,
251	        requested.model,
252	        [row["model"] for row in rows],
253	    )
254	    reasoning_summary = summarize_field(
255	        "reasoning_effort",
256	        requested.reasoning_effort,
257	        requested.reasoning_effort,
258	        [row["reasoning_effort"] for row in rows],
259	    )
260	    approval_summary = summarize_field(
261	        "approval_mode",
262	        requested.approval_mode,
263	        requested.approval_mode,
264	        [row["approval_mode"] for row in rows],
265	    )
266	    sandbox_summary = summarize_field(
267	        "sandbox_policy",
268	        requested_sandbox_display,
269	        requested_sandbox_key,
270	        [normalize_sandbox(row["sandbox_policy"])[1] for row in rows],
271	    )
272	
273	    lines = [
274	        "# Codex Launch Truth Capture",
275	        "",
276	        f"- `label`: {label}",
277	        f"- `captured_at`: {captured_at}",
278	        f"- `db_path`: {db_path}",
279	        f"- `selection`: {boundary_description}",
280	        "",
281	        "## Requested Settings",
282	    ]
283	
284	    requested_rows = requested.as_rows()
285	    if requested_rows:
286	        for setting, value in requested_rows:
287	            lines.append(f"- `{setting}`: {value}")
288	    else:
289	        lines.append("- No requested settings were supplied.")
290	
291	    lines.extend(
292	        [
293	            "",
294	            "## Effective Thread Rows",
295	            "",
296	            "| thread_id | created_at | model | reasoning_effort | approval_mode | sandbox_policy | agent_role | agent_path |",
297	            "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
298	        ]
299	    )
300	
301	    for row in reversed(rows):
302	        sandbox_display, _ = normalize_sandbox(row["sandbox_policy"])
303	        lines.append(
304	            "| {thread_id} | {created_at} | {model} | {reasoning_effort} | "
305	            "{approval_mode} | {sandbox_policy} | {agent_role} | {agent_path} |".format(
306	                thread_id=row["id"],
307	                created_at=format_local_timestamp(row["created_at"]),
308	                model=row["model"] or "-",
309	                reasoning_effort=row["reasoning_effort"] or "-",
310	                approval_mode=row["approval_mode"] or "-",
311	                sandbox_policy=sandbox_display or "-",
312	                agent_role=row["agent_role"] or "-",
313	                agent_path=row["agent_path"] or "-",
314	            )
315	        )
316	
317	    lines.extend(
318	        [
319	            "",
320	            "## Assessment",
321	            model_summary,
322	            reasoning_summary,
323	            approval_summary,
324	            sandbox_summary,
325	        ]
326	    )
327	
328	    if requested.agent:
329	        lines.append(
330	            "- `requested_agent`: preserved as operator-declared intent only. "
331	            "The current sqlite thread rows do not prove the named agent."
332	        )
333	
334	    if requested.agent_path:
335	        populated_agent_paths = [row["agent_path"] for row in rows if row["agent_path"]]
336	        if not populated_agent_paths:
337	            lines.append(
338	                "- `requested_agent_path`: unresolved. The current sqlite thread rows "
339	                "did not populate `agent_path`, so this capture cannot prove that "
340	                "specific config file reached the worker."
341	            )
342	        else:
343	            matches = sum(
344	                1 for path in populated_agent_paths if Path(path) == Path(requested.agent_path)
345	            )
346	            total = len(populated_agent_paths)
347	            if matches == total:
348	                lines.append(
349	                    "- `requested_agent_path`: matched across all captured rows that "
350	                    "reported `agent_path`."
351	                )
352	            else:
353	                lines.append(
354	                    "- `requested_agent_path`: mixed or mismatched across captured rows "
355	                    "that reported `agent_path`."
356	                )
357	
358	    if "latest" in boundary_description:
359	        lines.append(
360	            "- Selection caveat: `--latest` is weaker evidence than a pre-recorded "
361	            "`--since` boundary because unrelated recent worker launches can fall into "
362	            "the same capture."
363	        )
364	
365	    lines.append(
366	        "- This artifact records operator-declared requested settings beside effective "
367	        "thread rows. It does not replace reviewer judgment, and missing runtime fields "
368	        "must stay unresolved rather than being inferred."
369	    )
370	
371	    lines.append("")
372	    return "\n".join(lines)
373	
374	
375	def main() -> int:
376	    args = parse_args()
377	
378	    requested = RequestedSettings(
379	        model=args.requested_model,
380	        reasoning_effort=args.requested_reasoning,
381	        approval_mode=args.requested_approval,
382	        sandbox_policy=args.requested_sandbox,

385	    )

390	            "requested-versus-effective truth."
391	        )

393	    db_path = Path(args.db).expanduser()

396	
397	    since = parse_boundary(args.since) if args.since else None
398	    rows = fetch_threads(

403	    )

407

409	        f"worker threads created at or after {format_local_timestamp(since)}"
410	        if since is not None
411	        else f"latest {args.latest} worker thread(s)"
412	    )

414	    markdown = render_markdown(

Date: 2026-04-21
